bib.title: InternVL: Scaling up Vision Foundation Models and Aligning for Generic Visual-Linguistic Tasks
bib.venue: preprint (arXiv v3, 15 Jan 2024; the PDF prints no venue)

read.skipped: Reference list lines after [123] skimmed only; body, tables and all appendices read.

question: Can a vision encoder scaled to 6B parameters, progressively aligned with an LLM-initialised language middleware on web-scale image-text data, serve both contrastive and generative vision-language tasks?
hypothesis: Scaling the vision encoder to match LLM scale and aligning it with an LLM-initialised middleware (contrastive first, generative later) closes the parameter and representation gap that lightweight glue layers leave.
contributions: A large-scale vision-language foundation model aligning a 6B vision encoder with LLMs for the first time
A progressive image-text alignment strategy: contrastive on noisy web data, then generative on filtered data
Extensive comparison with state-of-the-art vision foundation models and VLLMs on 32 benchmarks

method.summary: InternViT-6B (vanilla ViT, 5.9B) plus QLLaMA (8B, multilingual LLaMA-7B with 96 queries and 1B new cross-attention params). Stage 1 contrastive training from scratch on 4.98B pairs, stage 2 generative training of only the new queries and cross-attention on 1.03B pairs, stage 3 SFT on ~4M instruction samples connecting to Vicuna or InternLM through an MLP.
method.task: vision-language foundation model pretraining; zero-shot classification, retrieval, captioning, multimodal dialogue

datasets.name: Stage 1/2 web image-text pairs (LAION-en, LAION-multi, LAION-COCO, COYO, Wukong, CC12M, CC3M, SBU)
datasets.size: 6.03B original; 4.98B after stage-1 cleaning (82.6%); 1.03B after stage-2 cleaning (17.0%)
datasets.preprocessing: Stage 1: minor filtering on CLIP similarity, watermark probability, unsafe probability, aesthetic score, image resolution, caption length; deduplicated against ImageNet-1K/22K, Flickr30K, COCO. Stage 2: caption filtering on length, completeness, readability, gibberish/boilerplate, offensive language, placeholder text, source code.

datasets.name: Stage 3 SFT mix
datasets.size: ~4M samples: captioning 588K, VQA 1.1M, OCR 294K, grounding 323K, grounded captioning 284K, conversation 1.4M
datasets.source: COCO Caption, TextCaps, VQAv2, OKVQA, A-OKVQA, IconQA, AI2D, GQA, OCR-VQA, ChartQA, DocVQA, ST-VQA, EST-VQA, InfoVQA, LLaVAR (20K), RefCOCO/+/g, Toloka, LLaVA-150K, SVIT, VisDial, LRV-Instruction, LLaVA-Mix-665K
datasets.preprocessing: converted to dialogue with LLaVA-1.5 response-format prompts

datasets.name: Evaluation sets
datasets.size: ImageNet-1K and variants, ObjectNet, 20 other classification sets, Kinetics 400/600/700, Flickr30K, COCO, Flickr30K-CN, COCO-CN, XTD, MSR-VTT, NoCaps, ADE20K, VQAv2, GQA, VizWiz, TextVQA, MME, POPE, Tiny LVLM
datasets.split: Karpathy test for COCO/Flickr30K captioning; NoCaps val; VQAv2/VizWiz test-dev; GQA test-balanced; TextVQA val; ADE20K val
datasets.preprocessing: Birdsnap: only 1,845 of 2,443 test images downloadable

models.name: QLLaMA
models.architecture: multilingual LLaMA-7B + 96 learnable queries + cross-attention layers
models.init_from: Cui et al. 2023 Chinese LLaMA/Alpaca multilingual LLaMA-7B

other.note: frozen LLM decoder in the QLLaMA configuration; MLP and QLLaMA trained

models.name: ViT-22B, OpenCLIP-G, EVA-02-CLIP-E+, BLIP-2, InstructBLIP, LLaVA-1.5, Qwen-VL and others

training.objective: Stage 1: CLIP symmetric cross-entropy contrastive loss. Stage 2: sum of ITC + ITM + ITG (BLIP-2 style). Stage 3: generative (SFT) loss
training.optimizer: AdamW; stage 1 betas 0.9/0.95; stage 2 betas 0.9/0.98; retrieval FT and ADE20K betas 0.9/0.999; linear probe SGD momentum 0.9
training.lr: stage 1 peak 1e-3 (image enc) and 1e-4 (text enc); stage 2 cross-attn 5e-5 with encoders frozen; retrieval FT 1e-6; ImageNet linear probe 0.2; ADE20K 4e-5
training.warmup: stage 1: 5K iterations; stage 2: 2K; retrieval FT: 100; linear probe: 1 epoch; ADE20K: 1.5K
training.batch_size: stage 1: 164K; stage 2: 20K; stage 3 QLLaMA config: 512; retrieval FT: 1024; linear probe: 1024; ADE20K: 16
training.epochs: stage 3 LLaVA recipe: 1 epoch per step; retrieval FT: 10; linear probe: 10
training.weight_decay: stage 1 0.1; stage 2 0.05; retrieval FT 0.05; linear probe 0.0; ADE20K 0.0/0.05/0.05
training.regularisation: drop path: stage 1 uniform 0.2, stage 2 0.0, retrieval FT 0.3, ADE20K full tuning 0.4; layer-wise lr decay 0.9 in retrieval FT (0.95 ADE20K full tuning); random resized crop; stage 1 masks 50% of image tokens at 196x196
training.hardware: stage 1: 640x A100 (80G); stage 2: 160x A100 (80G); retrieval FT: 32x A100; linear probe and ADE20K: 8x A100

other.input_resolution: stage 1: 196x196 (50% token masking) then 224x224 unmasked for the final 0.5B samples; stage 2: 224x224; retrieval FT 364x364; ADE20K 504x504
other.stage3: InternVL-Chat w/o QLLaMA: train MLP on LGS-558K then LLM on LLaVA-Mix-665K, one epoch each; w/ QLLaMA: MLP first then LLM on custom 4M SFT, batch 512; LLM decoder can stay frozen
other.linear_probe: extra BatchNorm on frozen features; average-pooled patch tokens concatenated with class token
other.throughput_note: no GPU-hours or total FLOPs of training given

inference.prompting: LLaVA-1.5 response-format prompts, e.g. 'Answer the question using a single word or phrase.' and 'Provide a one-sentence caption for the provided image.'

other.video: Kinetics: 1 center frame or 8 uniformly sampled frames; MSR-VTT 8 frames encoded independently and embeddings averaged
other.efficiency_test: batch 128, single A100, Flash Attention, bf16, PyTorch

evidence.quote: We measure the time cost with a batch size of 128 on a single A100 GPU. Flash Attention [35] and bf16 precision are used during testing.

results.table: Table 19, rows InternVL-C 224 and 448, column FPS

limits: Efficiency (Table 19) covers only 224, 336 and 448 px, encoding only (no LLM decoding), batch 128, one A100; no memory numbers, no accuracy-vs-resolution curve for the same model.
FPS in Table 19 is total image-plus-text pair encoding rate (includes 4.9 ms text), not image-encoder-only throughput.
The paper states timings are unoptimised (no quantisation or TensorRT).
Resolution effect on accuracy is not ablated; main-table models use 224 or 336 inputs, and Table 9 mixes resolution with glue layer, data and LLM changes.
No seeds, error bars or significance tests; no training compute in GPU-hours; stage-3 SFT hyperparameters (lr, steps) mostly not given.
Starred benchmarks saw their training annotations; several competitor numbers are not like-for-like in training data.
Superseded in practice by later InternVL releases (dynamic tiling); not covered here.
